The instruction representation has a documented relationship to textual PTX.
Unsupported syntax and features cannot silently execute as supported operations.

summary: Execute a bounded approximate base-two exponential with exact special cases, original operands, predicates, actual fetch and precise effects.
Preserve both named ULP policies and expose positive finite inputs as missing coverage in every existence guarantee.
remaining: The selected bounded fetched leaf is complete and independently checked. Positive finite exponential/overflow behavior, other forms, raw PTX parsing, whole kernels and hardware conformance remain outside this fragment. It is not counted as full accepted-form coverage.

from.quote:
The base-two exponential of x is 2 raised to the power x. This responsibility
covers a bounded fragment of ex2.approx.f32, using binary32 (32-bit floating
point), the pinned PTX 9.4 version and sm_20 or later. It preserves subnormal
numbers, the small representable values near zero, and excludes the optional
flush-to-zero mode. The typed text interface accepts exactly this spelling,
a word-register destination and one word operand; it is not a raw PTX parser.

passage.quote:
def SupportedTarget (target : Ptx.Target) : Prop :=
  target.isa = 94 ∧ 20 ≤ target.sm

from.quote:

The supported input domain consists of finite nonpositive values, both
infinities, and NaN (not a number). Both signs of zero produce exactly positive
one. Negative infinity produces positive zero; positive infinity produces
positive infinity. NaN permits any NaN output in the existing conservative
payload policy. For strictly negative finite inputs, every finite result in the
reviewed two-ULP neighborhood is retained. ULP means the spacing of the floating
point grid: the neighborhood uses the larger spacing at the nearest-even rounded
reference and at the returned value. This covers the two named conventions,
without claiming a unique interpretation of NVIDIA's wording or physical
realizability of every permitted bit pattern.

passage.quote:
def Results (input output : Word) : Prop :=
  (isNaN input = true ∧ isNaN output = true) ∨
  (input = 0xff800000 ∧ output = 0) ∨
  (input = 0x7f800000 ∧ output = 0x7f800000) ∨
  ∃ x : ℝ, finiteReal input = some x ∧ x ≤ 0 ∧
    if x = 0 then output = 0x3f800000 else ConservativeULP.Results ((2:ℝ)^x) output

passage.quote:
theorem negative_iff (input output : Word) (x : ℝ)
    (value : finiteReal input = some x) (negative : x < 0) :
    Results input output ↔ ConservativeULP.Results ((2:ℝ)^x) output := by
  rw [finite_iff input output x value]
  simp [negative.le, ne_of_lt negative]

theorem zero_iff (input output : Word) (value : finiteReal input = some 0) :

from.quote:
Positive finite operands have no enabled step in this fragment. This is missing
formalization coverage, not a claim that NVIDIA leaves their behavior undefined
or that a GPU cannot execute them. It must remain visible in every existence
contract. A disabled predicate skips even an unsupported input, without requiring
an arithmetic result. An enabled instruction reads its operand in the original
state, writes exactly its destination, and advances the instruction position.
Source and destination may be the same register. Other registers, predicates,
address registers and memory are preserved. The occurrence records the actual
instruction, position, reads and writes, with no memory access.

passage.quote:
inductive Eval (i : Instr) : Scalar.State → Scalar.State → Occurrence → Prop
  | skipped {s} (disabled : i.guard.eval s = false) :
      Eval i s {s with pc := s.pc + 1} (occurrence s i false)
  | executed {s value} (enabled : i.guard.eval s = true)
      (result : Ptx.Binary32.Exponential.Results (i.source.eval s) value) :
      Eval i s {{s with pc := s.pc + 1} with
        regs := Scalar.update s.regs i.destination value} (occurrence s i true)

passage.quote:
theorem eval_destination (i : Instr) (s next : Scalar.State) (event : Occurrence)
    (hEval : Eval i s next event) (enabled : i.guard.eval s = true) :
    Ptx.Binary32.Exponential.Results (i.source.eval s) (next.regs i.destination) := by
  cases hEval with
  | skipped disabled => simp [enabled] at disabled
  | executed _ result => simpa using result

theorem eval_frame (i : Instr) (s next : Scalar.State) (event : Occurrence)
    (hEval : Eval i s next event) :
    next.pc = s.pc+1 ∧ next.memory = s.memory ∧ next.addrs = s.addrs ∧ next.preds = s.preds := by
  cases hEval <;> simp_all

theorem eval_other (i : Instr) (s next : Scalar.State) (event : Occurrence) (other : Nat)
    (hEval : Eval i s next event) (different : other ≠ i.destination) :
    next.regs other = s.regs other := by
  cases hEval with
  | skipped _ => rfl
  | executed _ _ => simp [Scalar.update, different]

theorem eval_event (i : Instr) (s next : Scalar.State) (event : Occurrence)
    (hEval : Eval i s next event) : event = occurrence s i (i.guard.eval s) := by
  cases hEval with
  | skipped h => simp [h]
  | executed h _ => simp [h]

from.quote:
A program step requires actual fetch at the current instruction position and the
selected target. A next state exists exactly when the predicate is disabled or
the enabled operand is in the supported numerical domain. This is one-step
existence, not a whole-kernel termination or hardware progress guarantee.
For an enabled instruction, finite nonpositive input gives a finite output
with error at most 5*2^-24 from 2^x, including reference rounding. The actual destination also connects to the
natural-exponential base-conversion proof when preceded by its encoded multiply.
These numerical bounds do not replace source review, memory/storage contracts,
or proof of a parallel softmax program.

passage.quote:
theorem eval_exists_iff (i : Instr) (s : Scalar.State) :
    (∃ next event, Eval i s next event) ↔
      i.guard.eval s = false ∨ Ptx.Binary32.Exponential.Supported (i.source.eval s) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨next,event,h⟩
    cases h with
    | skipped h => exact Or.inl h
    | executed h result => exact Or.inr (Ptx.Binary32.Exponential.results_supported result)
  · exact eval_exists i s

passage.quote:
theorem step_exists (target : Ptx.Target) (program : List Instr) (s : Scalar.State)
    (i : Instr) (supported : SupportedTarget target) (fetch : program[s.pc]? = some i)
    (admissible : i.guard.eval s = false ∨
      Ptx.Binary32.Exponential.Supported (i.source.eval s)) :
    ∃ next event, Step target program s next event := by
  obtain ⟨next,event,he⟩ := eval_exists i s admissible
  exact ⟨next,event,supported,i,fetch,he⟩
